synthesis: Admin 'Login as Scout user' impersonation intermittently fails with NO error message. Observed 2026-09-16 during Premier Adjusters Scout demo: force-login worked earlier in the admin session, then stopped loading for 3 different Scout users consecutively. Filed day after PR #410 merge (2026-09-15) which fixed a related silent-failure issue (duplicate GET revoking live token). Root investigation must determine: (1) whether PR #410 introduced a regression for consecutive force-logins of different drivers within one admin session, (2) whether an active driver session interferes with admin force-login, (3) why the failure is silent (no 401/403/404 surfaced to UI). Product decision required on AC5: should force-login kick an active driver out of their own session?

scope.summary: Investigate and fix silent failure in Scout force-login flow when admin impersonates multiple Scout users consecutively OR when target driver has active session. Preserve PR #410 fixes (token pruning, session tracking, 401 surfacing). Add explicit error messaging for any intentional blocks.

proposed_changes.change: Review mintFor() session tracking - verify Session::push() doesn't accumulate stale IDs across consecutive force-logins of different drivers; consider scoping session array to driver ID or clearing on each mint
proposed_changes.reason: Session array 'clarity_scout_force_token_ids' could accumulate token IDs from User A when admin force-logins User B, causing revokeTracked() to wrongly revoke User A's token if triggered mid-session

proposed_changes.change: Add defensive checks: (1) verify token was successfully minted (not null), (2) log warning if driver already has KEEP_PER_DRIVER force tokens (suggests stale session), (3) return explicit error if assigned_user is null instead of 404 with message the UI might not show
proposed_changes.reason: Silent failure could occur if mintFor() returns empty/null token OR if view renders with malformed forceAuth; ticket reports NO error message reaching user

proposed_changes.change: Add fallback error handling if window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ exists but token/user/kit fields are missing/invalid - redirect to login with reason instead of silently booting broken state
proposed_changes.reason: If blade renders with null/malformed token, PWA boots but auth fails silently; need to surface this to admin

proposed_changes.change: Consider deferring revokeTracked() until AFTER session()->invalidate() if consecutive impersonations within same browser cause session array to persist stale IDs; OR clear force token session key explicitly before new impersonation
proposed_changes.reason: Line 32 calls revokeTracked() before line 35 invalidates session - if admin re-impersonates in same browser, old token IDs might still be in memory

proposed_changes.change: Add test: consecutive force-logins to 3 different drivers within same admin session without closing tabs; verify all 3 tokens remain valid and no cross-revocation occurs
proposed_changes.reason: Ticket reports exactly this failure scenario - 3 consecutive force-logins stopped working; no test coverage for this case
proposed_changes.ref: existing tests cover duplicate GET of same driver, not consecutive different drivers

questions.q: Was the Premier Adjusters demo environment running the PR #410 deploy (merged 2026-09-15) at time of incident (2026-09-16)?
Did the admin re-impersonate (go through Backyard /auth/impersonate) between the working force-login and the 3 failures, or was it all within one continuous impersonation session?
Were the 3 Scout users in the same org or different orgs? (Different orgs would require re-impersonation, same org would not)
Did the admin keep prior force-login tabs open while trying to force-login to subsequent users, or close each tab before opening next?
What exactly does 'stopped loading' mean - did the /scout/force-login/{kit} route return 403/404, OR did it return 200 with a rendered view that failed to boot the PWA?
Were any of the 3 target Scout users actively logged in on their own devices at the time admin tried to force-login?
Product decision: Should admin force-login (clarity-scout-force-token) kick out an active driver's normal session (clarity-scout-token), or should both coexist? Current code allows coexist.
Does normal driver login (ClarityScoutAuthController line 64) revoking ALL clarity-scout-token tokens interfere with force tokens? (Unlikely - different token names)
questions.answer: No - line 64 deletes where('name', 'clarity-scout-token') which does NOT match 'clarity-scout-force-token'; they coexist safely

questions.q: Does ScoutForceTokens::mintFor() Session::push() create a session array that accumulates across consecutive force-logins of different drivers?
questions.answer: Yes - line 49 Session::push(SESSION_KEY, token_id) appends to array; if admin force-logins Driver A then Driver B, array contains IDs for both; revokeTracked() would revoke BOTH if called mid-session

questions.q: When does revokeTracked() fire? Only on impersonation entry/exit, or anywhere else?
questions.answer: Three call sites: (1) ImpersonateController@impersonate line 32 (new impersonation), (2) @leave line 83, (3) @exitAdminMode line 94; NOT called on normal force-login flow

questions.q: Does PR #410 service worker change (lines 89-90 exclude /scout/force-login from caching) prevent the original issue from recurring?
questions.answer: Yes - force-login HTML embedding live token is no longer cached; CLEAR_API_CACHE also purges API responses; original PR #410 bug should not recur

notes: PR #410 commit 83fb68d24 merged 2026-09-15, ticket filed 2026-09-16 - suspicious timing suggests either (a) deploy introduced regression, (b) pre-410 session state conflicts with post-410 code, or (c) new edge case not covered by PR #410 tests
ScoutForceTokens keeps KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 tokens per driver to handle duplicate GET (prefetch/double-click); prunes expired + older than 3 on each mint
Force tokens tracked in admin's SESSION array under key 'clarity_scout_force_token_ids'; revokeTracked() pulls ALL IDs and deletes them - potential cross-driver revocation if array accumulates
Normal driver login deletes ALL 'clarity-scout-token' tokens (ClarityScoutAuthController line 64) but does NOT touch 'clarity-scout-force-token' - names differ intentionally so both can coexist

ImpersonateController@impersonate line 35 calls session()->invalidate() AFTER line 32 revokeTracked() - session array might persist in memory if admin re-impersonates in same browser without full logout

ClarityScoutForceLoginController line 16 abort_unless(session()->has('admin_impersonator'), 403) - if admin's session expires or admin_impersonator key is missing, returns 403 not 200; ticket says NO error so 403 path unlikely
Login.vue lines 8-14 display signedOut reason from sessionStorage (set by handleUnauthorized in fetch.js lines 83-106); if force-login page 401'd after loading, this should have fired
Scout PWA main.js lines 17-20 checks window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ and calls forceAuthenticate(); if payload is malformed/null, PWA might boot but fail silently - no error handling here

Existing tests cover: (1) duplicate GET of same driver keeps prior token alive, (2) prunes beyond KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3, (3) revokes on leave/exitAdminMode, (4) doesn't evict driver's normal token; MISSING: consecutive force-logins of different drivers in same session
Scout knowledge card (scout.md) warns about rapid iteration causing stale ticket assumptions; earlier QA-complete work already handled shift pollution on force-login
The isScoutForceImpersonator() pattern documents API-side guards; User model line 254 checks currentAccessToken abilities for 'clarity-scout-force'

grounding.code_flow: Admin clicks 'Login to Scout' in Filament → GET /scout/force-login/{kit} (new tab) → ClarityScoutForceLoginController checks admin_impersonator session → ScoutForceTokens::mintFor(driver) creates token + Session::push(token_id) → prune(driver) keeps 3 most recent → blade renders clarity-scout view with window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ = {token, user, kit, ...} → PWA main.js reads payload, calls auth.forceAuthenticate(data) → store sets token, connects Echo → app boots. REVOCATION: ImpersonateController entry/exit calls revokeTracked() which Session::pull() all tracked IDs and deletes those PersonalAccessTokens. FAILURE MODE: if session array accumulates IDs from Driver A when admin force-logins Driver B, subsequent revokeTracked() (on new impersonation or exit) would revoke Driver A's token even though Driver A's tab is still open.

escalate.reason: Auth/session is blast-radius - a bug here can lock users out or leak sessions. AC5 requires product decision (kick out active driver or allow coexist). Ticket filed day after PR #410 merge suggests either regression or edge case not covered by existing tests. Root cause hypothesis (Session::push accumulation + no payload validation) is medium-confidence; need human review of session lifecycle before committing to fix. Also need confirmation from user/PM on Premier demo environment state (was PR #410 deployed? were drivers actively logged in?). Recommend pairing with original PR #410 author (Dalton per commit) to ensure no regression.
